newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD's Muentefering calls for restart of tax talks.
newsitem.headline: SPD's Muentefering calls for restart of tax talks.

text.p: Franz Muentefering, party manager of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), on Friday called for a rapid resumption of the stalled tax reform talks with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition.
The Berlin daily newspaper B.Z. quoted Muentefering as saying, "The SPD is prepared to come to rapid conclusions that serve the fight against unemployment. Also to talks with the government parties."
Muentefering's comments appeared to be at odds with remarks made on Thursday by SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine, who said the SPD's return to the bargaining table depended on new proposals from Kohl.
The SPD boycotted a round of tax reform talks slated for last Saturday in protest against the government's plan to curtail coal subsidies.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel is to unveil his proposed tax reform legislation later on Friday.

Muentefering said it would be easily possible to cut unemployment insurance premiums by two percent immediately. But the SPD sees no way to finance a cut in the top tax rate, as proposed by the government.
